correctness.rationale: For every smooth complex cubic threefold and every triple line, the normal quadratic pencil is basepoint-free, hence has two distinct square members and admits diagonal normal form. The Fano-chart Jacobian is the identity; the dependent coordinates vanish at least cubically. The transverse-gradient determinant has exact quadratic initial form -6kef with k nonzero and Hessian determinant -36k^2. Formal Morse lemma gives a node; the published singular-support theorem excludes any other singularity. The standalone SymPy checker verified the pivotal polynomial identities for all general coefficients.

originality.rationale: Bockondas–Boissière Theorem 6 fixes precisely the singular support, but their Remark 9 explicitly leaves universal nodality open; the proof computes a universal nondegenerate quadratic tangent cone at every possible singular point. No covering statement appeared in checked sources; possible unindexed prior work remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible historical local-analytic proof might anticipate the universal node statement.

value.rationale: The theorem answers an explicit open question in Bockondas–Boissière Remark 9 for every smooth complex cubic threefold, rather than only generic or Fermat cases. It gives the previously unestablished node analytic type, reduced Jacobian singular scheme, delta and Tjurina invariants, and numerical genus consequences. These are structurally significant geometric information not implied by singular support or line counts.
